findings.title: findMany method removed without migration path
findings.body: The previously-public `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` method has been deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`. Any existing caller (other modules, route handlers, etc.) that previously invoked `service.findMany({ select, where, orderBy, take, ... })` will now fail to compile, and the README/PR description does not document this as a breaking change nor provide a migration shim. A search for other consumers should be done before merging and any callers must be updated to use `prisma.$queryRaw` with the returned conditions.

findings.title: Loss of where-clause merging capability
findings.body: The previous `findMany` merged a caller's `findManyArgs.where` into the final Prisma where (via `...findManyArgs.where, AND: [auth, filter]`). The new `getBaseConditions()` only returns the authorization + filter SQL fragment and provides no way for a caller to layer additional predicates. Any caller that relied on passing extra `where` (date ranges, status filters, paging cursor, etc.) will silently lose those filters. The integration test now hard-codes a `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"` query and the call sites have no documented API to add their own conditions.

findings.title: Caching behaviour no longer covered by tests
findings.body: The previous test file contained a `describe("Caching", ...)` block with two tests that verified `getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions` returned identical objects on repeated calls (proving the internal cache works). The new diff silently removes that entire describe block while the cache (`this.cachedAuthConditions`, `this.cachedFilterConditions`) is still implemented in the service. There is no replacement test, so regressions to the cache (e.g. accidental double work, or cache not invalidating after construction) would not be caught. The PR description does not mention removing this coverage.

findings.title: Integration test depends on BookingTimeStatusDenormalized being synchronously populated
findings.body: The integration test inserts rows via `prisma.booking.create` / `prisma.eventType.create` and immediately runs `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${baseConditions}`, expecting the just-inserted booking to appear. This relies on `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` being kept in sync with `Booking` synchronously (via trigger or denormalization job at insert time). If it is a materialized view or is only refreshed by a background job, this test will be flaky in CI. The PR description even acknowledges that the test runner had configuration issues and asks for manual verification. There is no setup/teardown that guarantees the denormalized table reflects the freshly created booking, and no assertion that the table is non-empty before running the test.

findings.title: Prisma.Sql equality assertions are fragile and not validated
findings.body: Every assertion in the rewritten test compares the service output with a literal `Prisma.sql\`...\`` template using `expect(...).toEqual(...)`. `Prisma.Sql` is an object whose internal `strings` / `values` arrays are sensitive to whitespace, parenthesis placement, and the order of interpolation. Several assertions in the diff (e.g. line 273, 296-298, 333-343) embed `${[array]}` exactly matching the implementation's array order; if the implementation ever produces a different equivalent SQL (e.g. `("teamId" = ANY($1))` vs `("teamId" = $1)` for a single element, or different spacing) the tests will fail even though the SQL is semantically identical. There is no helper that compares the rendered SQL structurally, and the PR description explicitly flags that the tests were not actually run (`test runner configuration issues`) so the equality assumptions are unverified.

findings.title: Constructor type widened without enforcing teamId for team scope
findings.body: The constructor parameter type changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (discriminated union that requires `teamId` when `scope === "team"`) to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `teamId` is optional. `safeParse` then sets `this.options = null` on any validation failure, which silently downgrades the user to `NOTHING_CONDITION` (no results) instead of throwing. A caller that passes `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` will get a service that returns nothing with no error. This is a behaviour change: previously TypeScript would reject the call at compile time; now it silently produces empty results, which is a security/visibility concern since it may mask authorization bugs.

findings.title: PR description mislabels the scope of the change
findings.body: The PR title and description say this only "updates the integration tests for the Prisma.sql format that was previously converted in the service implementation", but the diff also substantially rewrites the service itself: deletes `findMany`, changes return types from `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql`, widens the constructor options type, removes the `NOTHING = { id: -1 }` sentinel, and adds `getBaseConditions()`. Reviewers reading the description would not expect these breaking service-level changes. The description should be updated to call out the API break and the removal of cache tests.
